requirements: Per-surface native acceptance and DOSBox regression evidence
Qualified same-input observable comparisons, with declared semantic differences
Real OS/driver/game compatibility evidence beyond bare-metal fixtures
Cold restore/restart and fallback rehearsal; never load a DOSBox native state as QEMU state
Retain DOSBox selectable after QEMU becomes the default

status_legend.partial: Native machinery or reused host code exists with material semantic/API gaps; no parity claim
status_legend.pending: No native equivalent in the audited starting revision
status_legend.retained_host_code: Independent host/static code remains; rerun affected integration witnesses
status_legend.planned_addition_not_legacy_capability: Discussed addition, not an existing capability that a method inventory can certify

qualification_notice: Source inventory and test references are not evidence of runtime parity. Qualification is explicit per surface and compatibility campaign.

slices.title: Owned QEMU lifecycle and CPU controls
slices.gate: Explicit backend selection, bounded transport, process cleanup, stopped inspection, physical/virtual RAM, guarded registers/RAM, native breakpoint/watchpoint and stored capture; retain DOSBox choices.
scope_limits: Machine context is available; this does not establish DOS source-address mapping, legacy reply schema, guest process lifecycle or drop-in parity.

Raw MachineContext.run is host-time bounded and returns machine stops. The COM/MZ process session separately verifies parent return for guest_exit/guest_tsr; neither path supplies guest_ms/fast_forward/stop_on_hook semantics.
Raw native QEMU exposes one machine context. dosbox-qemu exposes a DOS CPU plus its surrounding Linux machine; those are different CPUs and cannot be renamed into one native DOS context.

The legacy public DOS route intentionally refuses direct writes (use RAM layers, runtime bindings or edited checkpoints); machine context already permits explicit guarded edits. Preserve legacy refusal and expose new context semantics explicitly.
qemu-machine has its own explicit bounded script grammar and operation set. The full legacy DOS script vocabulary is not supported merely because script() exists.

slices.title: Actual DOS boot, source-bound programs and resident drivers
slices.gate: Boot a real DOS image; admit supplied COM/MZ bytes; observe relocation/PSP/entry, child/parent termination and TSR distinction; pin guest profile and observed task/page mappings.
scope_limits: Original COM/MZ projects launch through real DOS EXEC with a separate private boot disk. Observed PSP/MCB, ordered MZ relocations, exact loader stack writes and native entry establish the initial source map; controls retain machine addresses.

Nonce-bound parent return and DOS AH=4Dh distinguish selected process exit/residency. Resident mappings intersect observed retained allocations; machine close and uncertain observations invalidate live ownership and capture epochs.
Entry requires observed real mode. Patched versions, secondary executable stubs, DPMI/V86 process mapping and real QEMM/DESQview scheduler/driver combinations remain unqualified.

Device-header registration and an authored SYS initialization marker qualify only those observations, not arbitrary device I/O. Game assets/drivers must already be present in the image; existing startup/configuration bytes are preserved.

slices.title: Observed execution traces and event searches
slices.gate: Compare explicit trace semantics, instruction/context/mode identity, callback-safe boundaries, new-page/new-region/register predicates, IRQ/fault/REP cases, and action causality.
scope_limits: QEMU records stopped native intervals with the observed read-only IRQ/timer stepping policy. Faults and partial REP can return normal debug stops; architectural retirement remains unknown.

Original real-mode COM/MZ captures verify instruction bytes, PSP/MCB ownership and the initial epoch. Canonical source sites account for ordered MZ relocations and exact loader writes; persistent event searches rederive identity from original source and ordered entry/artifact receipts.

Unsupported source bytes, module departures, allocation/epoch or mode changes stop the source binding. An unbound final observation cannot close a source window or narrow absence. Live overlay rebinding, protected/V86 tasks, input-to-source-trace causality and whole-program timing remain unqualified.
Raw machine traces remain separately available and do not acquire a DOS process source map. Streaming fetch capture/cursors are not supplied by bounded stopped observations.

slices.title: Guest clock, coherent media and physical input
slices.gate: Guest-time bounded runs, last-completed-frame ownership, stale-frame refusal, keyboard make/break and held leases, mouse-driver consumption/release, frame-edge input and device timing.
scope_limits: Explicit standard and instruction profiles preserve stock QEMU behavior. The opt-in virtual profile requires the fDisBull API1 extension on QEMU10.0.13 and observes QEMU_CLOCK_VIRTUAL directly, separately from query-replay.icount and host time.

Virtual-profile initial real-mode COM/MZ source traces advertise source_trace_clock and retain optional fdisbull-source-clock-1 brackets. Before/after native time, counter and epoch must remain identical across ownership/register/instruction observation. This uses the existing native clock extension, not a new QEMU patch or automatic timing synchronization.

virtual-time-range predicates require exact run, host epoch and native epoch plus half-open integer start_ns/end_ns bounds. Live and saved-script requests check every clock leaf before execution and earlier script mutations. Literal identities come from an earlier request; trace-until result interpolation remains unsupported. A time predicate observes debugger boundaries rather than an exact native timer cutoff.

Stored query rows and search witnesses retain validated source clocks; optional endpoint_clock preserves a count trace's final boundary without adding an N+1 event. Reopened artifacts bind native admission and source lineage, enforce homogeneous stable brackets and monotonic time/counter/sequence order. Candidate source identity remains independent of timestamps. Missing or foreign clocks are unknown offline; malformed clocks are rejected for every query.

Source-clock joins establish observation order within one run and both epochs, not input causation, natural instruction latency, guest consumption or completed guest frames. Equal nanoseconds do not establish callback order; observed GDB IRQ/timer policy remains in force. An unbound final time match leaves source_window_closed false. Source-trace host bounds include lock admission and persistence; late or failed storage retains known stop evidence and any artifact IDs in error.result without replay.

clock_advance uses one native timer and one GDB continue under a single host deadline. Token-bound requested/fired/stopped timestamps preserve early debugger/process stops and unknown input consumption; uncertain arm/cleanup closes the machine. No exact arbitrary-nanosecond cutoff, cycle accuracy, generic guest_ms, completed-frame or DOSBox timing parity claim.

The I/O witnesses use an explicit FreeDOS SWITCHES=/F baseline to omit its boot-key delay for the declared clock profiles. Production preserves caller configurations; guest boot delays may exceed a host startup budget under instruction counting.

By default, owned keyboard and relative PS/2 mouse edges queue while stopped, dispatch at most once during bounded GDB continue, and preserve its original stop reply. QMP acceptance is not guest consumption; an early stop may leave unsent edges pending. Legacy timed presses, frame-edge input, pixel clicks and INT33 driver parity remain unsupported.

Optional native input API1 on the explicit virtual profile adds input_schedule(delta_ns) and input_schedule_observe(), with debug-input-schedule/debug-input-schedule-observe retained JSON and input-schedule/input-schedule-observe script routes. The QEMU10.0.13 input patch applies after the current clock and media patches. virtual_input_schedule requires discovered native commands; timed_input, guest_time_control and completed_guest_frames stay false.

Scheduled arm/query are passive. The caller explicitly chooses one bounded run or clock_advance; the native virtual timer dispatches one token-owned batch through selected PS/2 callbacks and one final sync. The receipt binds requested start/deadline, actual dispatch/terminal time, lateness, sequence/count and epoch. Device FIFO acceptance, guest consumption, release and frame recognition remain unknown; no legacy guest_ms or exact cycle/frame-press parity.

The first actual stop cancels an unfired input timer and preserves the original breakpoint/watchpoint or DOS exit/TSR. Pending stops and equal/reached owned clock-budget deadlines win independently of timer insertion order. Pending edges require explicit input_schedule reschedule under a new token or input_cancel_pending disarm/discard before another run or queue mutation; no automatic continuation or replay. Scheduled runs and scripts bound post-stop reconciliation and evidence persistence by their host deadline.

Native scheduling admits 1..256 events, delay 1..60000000000 ns without signed overflow, relative X/Y values -32767..32767 and one edge per left/middle/right mouse button. Existing input ownership is bounded to 64 leases. Token history permits 4096 successful arms per process. Reset, epoch/profile loss or unsupported runstates invalidate the scheduler; migration stays blocked after its first successful arm. Terminal receipts freeze; uncertain native or evidence results close the VM. Timing auto-sync, host pacing and adaptive correction remain deferred.

capture_surface and screenshot retain PNG bytes, unique observation identity and a stopped selected-CPU/clock bracket. They do not establish a last-completed guest frame, freshness, scanline/IRQ phase, audio timing or UI readiness.

Held leases belong to the owned machine and invalidate on close. Cancellation only discards unsent transitions after proving native disarm; dispatched holds still need explicit release. Cancelling a queued release retains that hold. Unknown delivery or failed input evidence closes the VM without replay.
Periodic memory rules and scene/frame workflows still require qualified guest-time control. No host timer is relabeled as a guest-time scheduler.

The optional native media extension retains completed synchronous renderer updates under explicit virtual observation cadence, with immutable RGB pixels, token/update identity, publication time, age and stale-update refusal. A completed renderer update can contain partial guest drawing; completed_guest_frame and guest_frame_id remain unknown. No VBlank or full guest-mode-epoch parity.

Explicit qemu_audio=pc-speaker configures only the PC speaker with a none audiodev. Bounded 32000-Hz mono u8 callback output has sample ranges and delivery timestamps, overflow accounting and stopped WAV exports. Inactive intervals are not synthesized; PCM duration is not elapsed guest time or device queue drain. Other sound devices and audible playback are unqualified.

Media windows require locally owned tokens and a valid native clock epoch. After stop, retained evidence freezes; reset invalidates and migration after use is blocked. Reads and exports never run or flush the guest. Timing auto-sync, host pacing and adaptive correction are explicitly deferred.

After native clock admission, idle warping is suppressed for stopping/stopped CPUs even without an armed budget. An authored one-NOP ordinary GDB continue exposed an approximately 55-ms false jump to the PIT timer before this correction; genuinely halted CPUs remain eligible for virtual timer advances.

The optional retrace API1 patch follows the exact clock/media/input chain. Explicit qemu_retrace=precise with virtual clock selects standard PCI VGA and qemu-vga-precise-fdisbull-v1. retrace_observe, debug-retrace-observe and script retrace-observe are passive stopped reads; the default standard retrace profile retains ordinary QEMU behavior.

Retrace receipts bind run, host/native clock epochs, exact device/console/head, raw and cached model timing, stable stopped brackets and a monotone timing_generation. Write-time CR10/VBE coherence and generation hooks expose A-to-B-to-A transitions between observations. Generation is timing provenance, not a complete video-mode, palette, pixel-format or application identity.

Only initialized legacy VGA with VBE disabled and supported positive nonwrapped timing has phase evidence. Uninitialized/VBE/invalid timing returns an explicit unsupported reason without inventing a phase. The model vertical-retrace interval is not the entire vertical blank interval; synthesized status bits do not establish visible scanout, frame completion, input consumption or hardware-cycle accuracy.

Retrace queries do not read the guest status port, reset the attribute flip-flop, refresh pixels, advance clocks or wait for an edge. Admission pins the device and blocks migration. Reset or malformed/contradictory native evidence invalidates ownership. A current retrace sample cannot assign phase or generation to an older renderer publication.

Retrace host deadlines include lock admission, clock brackets and persistence; script capability/literal-timeout preflight precedes earlier writes. A late journal can commit before timeout failure; error.result retains the observation. Edge scheduling, automatic waits, timing auto-sync and default promotion remain unqualified.

slices.title: Native checkpoints, Anchor Stones and restore epochs
slices.gate: Whole CPU/device/clock/disk state, explicit mutable-file policy, cold-session restore, exact source/backend/profile identity, pending input policy, epoch invalidation, and close on uncertain restore.
scope_limits: MachineContext advertises save_states=False. DOSBox native sav files are not QEMU VM states; exact backend/profile, disk effects, input, layers, epochs and cold-session restore require a new qualified adapter.

slices.title: RAM/fetch layers, live code views, hooks and block services
slices.gate: Distinct RAM/fetch visibility, guarded all-or-nothing transitions, active precedence, translated-block invalidation, self-modifying code, callback context, declared host-effect authority and region-join contracts.
scope_limits: MachineContext advertises code_layers=False. A QEMU RAM write or PC redirect is not a fetch-only overlay; translated-block cache coherence and underlying-RAM self-modification guards require qualification.

slices.title: Checkpoint rewind, CPU/RAM deltas, frame history and trials
slices.gate: Unrecorded-mutation invalidation, partial-state freeze/recovery, file identity, bounded storage, full-frame/key restore, dependency-aware history and incomplete-trial refusal.
scope_limits: History consumers depend on separately qualified checkpoint, trace, input and layer contracts. CPU/RAM projection undo is partial and must preserve the frozen-state guard; epochs and disk/file policy cannot be inferred.

slices.title: Scenes, scripts, player workflows and analysis consumers
slices.gate: Coherent observation bundles, named actions, exact input ownership, scripts/budgets, frame/domain/readiness guards, spatial/fair-play policy and actual scene progression.
scope_limits: Host algorithms can be reused after their input/frame/state/control dependencies are qualified. Registering a method or importing a mixin does not supply those dependencies.

slices.title: Compatibility matrix, comparison and retained fallback
slices.gate: Real DOS/QEMM/DESQview/game cases and separate Windows regression; compare qualified observables and preserve DOSBox selectable after any default switch.
